origins.section: Carry-Over Is a Variable Linking Each Year to the Next
A Cap on Carry-Over and a Cap on a Window Are More Rows on the Same Expressions
Unspent Money Lapses, So the Cash Row Is an Inequality

gates.says: all 3 of this quiz's answerable readings held and each was taken over the question as it stands

recorded.prompt:q-carry-var: Read the whole lesson page, then this question. Using only what the page states, which option does the page decide is correct? Quote or cite the deciding passage.
recorded.pass:q-carry-var: page reader (independent agent; saw the lesson pages and the question)
recorded.outcome:q-carry-var: "The carried amounts are one of many equally good choices; another solver run may move money between years and keep the same NPV, so never report them as 'the' carry-over without fixing a rule for ties"
recorded.prompt:q-cap: Read the whole lesson page, then this question. Using only what the page states, which option does the page decide is correct? Quote or cite the deciding passage.
recorded.pass:q-cap: page reader (independent agent; saw the lesson pages and the question)
recorded.outcome:q-cap: "The window cap ... then costs more than the carry-over gave: the plan ends below the no-carry-over plan. That is a normal result, and the kind a planner needs to see as a table of scenarios"
recorded.prompt:q-lapse: Read the whole lesson page, then this question. Using only what the page states, which option does the page decide is correct? Quote or cite the deciding passage.
recorded.pass:q-lapse: page reader (independent agent; saw the lesson pages and the question)
recorded.outcome:q-lapse: "With a cap on carry-over, an equation forces the plan to spend at least 90% of each year's money, whether there is anything worth funding or not. Under the window cap that cannot be done: == instead of <= INFEASIBLE"

recorded.prompt:q-carry-var:a: Using only what the lesson page states, does a passage of the page rule this option out? Cite the passage, or say none does or that the option is partly true. Be strict.
recorded.pass:q-carry-var:a: page reader (independent agent; saw the lesson pages and the question)
recorded.outcome:q-carry-var:a: Equally good choices are expected, not a bug: "one of many equally good choices".
recorded.prompt:q-carry-var:c: Using only what the lesson page states, does a passage of the page rule this option out? Cite the passage, or say none does or that the option is partly true. Be strict.
recorded.pass:q-carry-var:c: page reader (independent agent; saw the lesson pages and the question)
recorded.outcome:q-carry-var:c: "the same schedule can carry different amounts"; carried amounts are not unique.
recorded.prompt:q-carry-var:d: Using only what the lesson page states, does a passage of the page rule this option out? Cite the passage, or say none does or that the option is partly true. Be strict.
recorded.pass:q-carry-var:d: page reader (independent agent; saw the lesson pages and the question)
recorded.outcome:q-carry-var:d: "Rolling money forward is worth $1,889k of NPV on the small portfolio"
recorded.prompt:q-cap:b: Using only what the lesson page states, does a passage of the page rule this option out? Cite the passage, or say none does or that the option is partly true. Be strict.
recorded.pass:q-cap:b: page reader (independent agent; saw the lesson pages and the question)
recorded.outcome:q-cap:b: "That is a normal result" - the lower NPV comes from the cap, not a mis-written cap.
recorded.prompt:q-cap:c: Using only what the lesson page states, does a passage of the page rule this option out? Cite the passage, or say none does or that the option is partly true. Be strict.
recorded.pass:q-cap:c: page reader (independent agent; saw the lesson pages and the question)
recorded.outcome:q-cap:c: "That is a normal result"; carry-over still adds plans, the cap removes more.
recorded.prompt:q-cap:d: Using only what the lesson page states, does a passage of the page rule this option out? Cite the passage, or say none does or that the option is partly true. Be strict.
recorded.pass:q-cap:d: page reader (independent agent; saw the lesson pages and the question)
recorded.outcome:q-cap:d: "the kind a planner needs to see as a table of scenarios rather than as one number" - a lower NPV is a scenario result, not grounds to drop the cap.
recorded.prompt:q-lapse:a: Using only what the lesson page states, does a passage of the page rule this option out? Cite the passage, or say none does or that the option is partly true. Be strict.
recorded.pass:q-lapse:a: page reader (independent agent; saw the lesson pages and the question)
recorded.outcome:q-lapse:a: The equation forces spending ("forces the plan to spend at least 90%"), not carrying.
recorded.prompt:q-lapse:c: Using only what the lesson page states, does a passage of the page rule this option out? Cite the passage, or say none does or that the option is partly true. Be strict.
recorded.pass:q-lapse:c: page reader (independent agent; saw the lesson pages and the question)
recorded.outcome:q-lapse:c: With <= the same caps give a feasible plan ("plus 2030-31 cap NPV $24,081k"); infeasibility comes from the equation.
recorded.prompt:q-lapse:d: Using only what the lesson page states, does a passage of the page rule this option out? Cite the passage, or say none does or that the option is partly true. Be strict.
recorded.pass:q-lapse:d: page reader (independent agent; saw the lesson pages and the question)
recorded.outcome:q-lapse:d: "Budget that is neither spent nor carried returns to the utility" - leftover above the cap may lapse under <=, which is feasible; the equation is the fault.
